title: Costco Barely Profits From Its Products. So How Does It Make $9 Billion?

shorts.title: Why Costco's $1.50 hot dog never gets more expensive
shorts.headline: The hot dog that hasn't changed price since the 80s
shorts.narration: A hot dog and a soda at Costco still cost one dollar fifty, the same price as in the nineteen eighties. Inflation should have pushed it far higher. So why doesn't Costco raise it? Because the hot dog isn't the product. You are. Costco makes its money when you renew your membership, and in the US and Canada, about ninety two percent of members do, every single year. A cheap hot dog is a tiny cost to keep that habit alive.
